page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-384-lssd is a high-capacity x86_64 general-purpose instance designed for demanding computational and storage-bound applications. The configuration provides 384 dedicated vCPUs and 1488 GB of RAM, yielding an operational density of 3.88 GB of memory per core. The instance includes 12,885 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage distributed across 32 individual disks, offering massive local drive capacity without reliance on remote network-attached volumes. No discrete GPU acceleration hardware is included in this profile.

With 384 dedicated cores and extensive local NVMe storage, this server delivers substantial parallel CPU capacity and high local disk throughput. The dedicated core allocation avoids CPU contention during multi-threaded execution. The local storage architecture requires deliberate planning, as local NVMe drives provide high performance but ephemeral persistence, necessitating application-level replication or external backups to preserve state across instance terminations. Additionally, networking configurations must account for zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The instance delivers high resource density by combining hundreds of physical compute threads with nearly 13 TB of local NVMe storage inside a single host environment. This consolidation offers qualitative efficiency for architectures that can maximize local high-IOPS storage alongside parallel processing, eliminating multi-node network overhead. Best-fit deployments include large-scale distributed NoSQL datastores, relational databases requiring extensive local scratch storage, real-time analytics pipelines, and distributed search indexing engines.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4d-standard-384-lssd is a high-density general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. The server incorporates 384 dedicated vCPUs alongside 1488 GB of system memory, maintaining an allocation ratio of 3.88 GB per core. A primary architectural component is its integrated storage array, which delivers 12,885 GB of local NVMe SSD space across 32 disks. The instance operates without discrete GPU accelerators and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Combining dense core counts with large-scale direct-attached NVMe storage provides qualitative efficiency for multi-threaded tasks requiring immediate high-throughput I/O. The absence of persistent default storage on the local drives requires data replication across nodes. The platform fits large database engines, high-speed indexing systems, big data processing pipelines, and enterprise-grade analytics workloads.
